reconverted_2026_11_07.why: act_convert.py dropped every Word <w:sym> character, which is how the register writes some characters in the Symbol and Wingdings fonts, and kept text typed in the Symbol font as private-use code points (U+F0xx) that display as empty boxes. act_convert_sym.py maps Symbol-font characters to Unicode (F0D7 ·, F0B4 ×, F02D −, F0B7 •, F0A3 ≤, F0B3 ≥, F0B0 °, F0A2 ′, F0BE —, F0B8 ÷, F0B1 ±, F020 space) and Wingdings boxes to "[ ]".
reconverted_2026_11_07.what_changed: Only bullets. 161 list bullets written as Symbol F0B7 <w:sym> had been dropped and are restored as "• " after the line's indent; 422 bullets kept as U+F0B7 are now "•"; one Symbol-font space kept as U+F020 (r 5534 note, line 13088) is now an ordinary space. 584 lines change; no line is added or removed. No decimal point, ×, −, ≤ or ≥ was lost. The notice header is kept exactly; a diff against the first deposit shows no other change.
reconverted_2026_11_07.encodings_affected: none changed: baseline-2026-11 reads the lists in r 1125 (1) and r 1126 (1) (lines 3424-3427, 3433-3436), whose words were intact (only the bullet was a private-use code point); no rule, case, value or finding relied on a lost character
